question: What is the main goal of a shift handover in the ward?

options.A: To assign daily cleaning duties to staff
options.B: To ensure continuity of care between shifts
options.C: To evaluate the performance of junior nurses
options.D: To write formal entries for patient case notes

explanation: Spot on! Handover is all about passing the baton smoothly so patient care never skips a beat when the shift changes. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T5#GNS112_U3_T5_h1)

question: Why is a proper shift report so important for keeping patients safe?

options.A: It reduces the total number of hospital working hours
options.B: It eliminates the need for doctors to write prescriptions
options.C: It prevents dangerous information gaps about patient status
options.D: It allows nurses to avoid direct patient bedside contact

explanation: You got it! Sharing clear updates means nothing important slips through the cracks, keeping your patients safe and sound. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T5#GNS112_U3_T5_h1)

question: Which handover style lets the patient join in and hear their own report?
explanation: Exactly! Doing handover right at the bedside lets patients talk, ask questions, and be part of their own healthcare journey. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T5#GNS112_U3_T5_h2)

question: What is the biggest downside of relying only on tape-recorded handovers?

options.A: It takes significantly longer than verbal reports
options.C: Staff cannot ask immediate questions for clarification
options.D: Patients find the recordings too loud to sleep

explanation: Spot on! Recordings are a one-way street—you can't pause a tape to ask 'Wait, what happened next?' like you can with a live colleague. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T5#GNS112_U3_T5_h2)

question: Which detail is an absolute must-mention when talking about patient safety during handover?
explanation: You nailed it! Highlighting allergies and fall risks right away stops accidental harm before the new shift even starts. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T5#GNS112_U3_T5_h3)

question: Why must you always mention pending lab tests during your shift report?

options.A: To decide which laboratory technicians stay overtime
options.B: To prove to doctors that nurses completed their duties
options.C: To ensure incoming nurses follow up on critical results
options.D: To calculate the daily hospital laboratory budget

explanation: Correct! Mentioning pending tests makes sure the incoming team chases up those results so no diagnosis gets delayed. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T5#GNS112_U3_T5_h3)

question: In the SBAR communication tool, what does the letter 'A' stand for?
explanation: Well done! 'A' stands for Assessment—your professional take on what is currently going on with the patient. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T5#GNS112_U3_T5_h4)

question: A nurse tells the incoming shift about a patient's past surgeries. Which SBAR category is this?
explanation: Spot on! Past medical history gives the background story that helps explain the patient's present condition. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T5#GNS112_U3_T5_h4)

question: What should you do with your rough handover notes at the end of a shift?

options.A: Dispose of them securely by shredding
options.B: Throw them into the general ward dustbin
options.C: Leave them neatly on the nurses' station desk
options.D: Take them home to study patient diagnoses

explanation: You got it! Patient info is strictly confidential, so rough notes must always go straight into the shredder. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T5#GNS112_U3_T5_h5)

question: Why is giving a patient handover out loud in a busy hospital hallway a bad idea?

options.A: It violates hospital policies regarding staff lunch break schedules
options.B: It makes it difficult for the incoming nurses to take handwritten notes
options.C: It prevents doctors from writing new medical prescription charts
options.D: It breaches patient confidentiality by exposing private data to outsiders

explanation: Spot on! Hallways have ears—keeping patient details private is a core part of professional nursing ethics. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T5#GNS112_U3_T5_h5)

question: Which of these is a common headache when trying to have a good shift handover?

options.A: Having too many standardized reporting tools
options.B: Active participation of the patient in bed

explanation: True that! A noisy, busy ward makes it super hard to focus and catch all the important clinical details. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T5#GNS112_U3_T5_h6)

question: What is the biggest risk of rushing through your shift handover?

options.A: Hospital management will reward the team for high efficiency
options.B: Critical clinical details may be missed, endangering the patient
options.C: The nursing staff will finish their shift duties much earlier
options.D: Incoming nurses will automatically remember all missing facts

explanation: You nailed it! Rushing leads to missed warnings, and in nursing, a missed detail can put a patient in real danger. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T5#GNS112_U3_T5_h6)
